[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The Lambda function has VPC configuration when subnets are supplied, but it can be created before the VPC execution policy is attached to its role. Ensure the VPC execution policy attachment is complete before creating the function so Lambda can initialize its VPC networking.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Lambda function conditionally uses VPC subnets/security groups, but it can be created before the VPC execution policy is attached. Ensure the VPC execution role policy attachment is complete before creating the VPC-configured function so its networking permissions are available.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Lambda function can be configured with VPC networking, but its execution role's VPC access policy attachment is not ordered before function creation. When VPC subnets are configured, ensure the attachment is in place before the function is created so Lambda has the required network-interface permissions.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`aws_lambda_function.webhook` attaches a VPC configuration (`vpc_config` from `var.config.lambda_subnet_ids`/`lambda_security_group_ids`), and Lambda needs the `AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole` managed policy on its execution role *at creation time* to create the ENIs (else creation fails with "The provided execution role does not have permissions to call CreateNetworkInterface"). Nothing in the function references `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role`, so Terraform may create the function in parallel with/before the attachment, making applies order-dependent. Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role]` to the function.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`aws_lambda_function.webhook` only references `aws_iam_role.webhook_lambda.arn`, so Terraform creates the function and `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role` concurrently (both only depend on the role). When `var.config.lambda_subnet_ids` is set the function gets a `vpc_config`, and Lambda creates the ENIs at function-creation time using the execution role; if the `AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole` policy has not been attached yet (and propagated), the apply fails with "The provided execution role does not have permissions to call CreateNetworkInterface". The provider documentation's own Lambda example wires this ordering explicitly (`depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.lambda_logs, ...]`). `aws_lambda_function.webhook` needs an explicit `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role]`; there is no attribute on the function that can carry this ordering implicitly.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
When VPC config is present, aws_lambda_function.webhook requires its role to carry the AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole permissions at creation, but Terraform only orders it against the role itself, not against the conditional aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role. The provider docs explicitly recommend depends_on from the function onto the role policy attachment for exactly this case.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_lambda_function.webhook configures vpc_config (when var.config.lambda_subnet_ids/lambda_security_group_ids are set) but does not depend on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role. Lambda function creation with VPC config requires the execution role to already carry the EC2 CreateNetworkInterface/DescribeNetworkInterfaces permissions granted by AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole; if the function is created before the attachment, CreateFunction can fail. Both resources are gated on the same var.config conditions, so the attachment always exists when vpc_config is set — the missing ordering just needs a bare depends_on (the attachment is counted and offers no attribute to reference).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_lambda_function.webhook can be created with a vpc_config block (when var.config.lambda_subnet_ids is non-empty), but it has no dependency on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role. AWS validates the execution role's EC2 networking permissions (AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole) at function-creation time; without ordering the count-gated policy attachment before the function, a fresh apply can fail with "the provided execution role does not have permissions to call CreateNetworkInterface" due to IAM propagation lag. Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role]` to the function.

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_cloudwatch_log_group.webhook is forced to be created AFTER aws_lambda_function.webhook because its name references aws_lambda_function.webhook.function_name. AWS Lambda auto-creates the /aws/lambda/<function_name> log group when the function is provisioned/first invoked, so the explicit log group (with its retention/kms/class settings) can collide with the auto-created one (ResourceAlreadyExistsException) — especially since both resources are subject to replacement via replace_triggered_by on null_resource.github_app_parameters. The function should be created after the log group (per the official aws_lambda_function docs: "Ensure log group exists before function"). Fixing this requires computing the log group name from var.config.prefix instead of the function attribute, and ordering the function after the log group; no single attribute reference on the function can express it cleanly (adding logging_config.log_group = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.webhook.name would be an option but also requires renaming the log group, so a bare depends_on on the function is the pragmatic fix).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
The dependency between aws_lambda_function.webhook and aws_cloudwatch_log_group.webhook runs in the wrong direction: the log group's `name` references the function's `function_name`, so the log group is only created after the function. The provider documentation recommends the log group exist before the function ("Ensure log group exists before function"); otherwise, if the function is invoked before the managed log group is created (or if the log group is replaced/destroyed while the function persists), Lambda auto-creates an unmanaged log group and the configured retention_in_days/kms_key_id/log_group_class are silently not applied. Note that a bare `depends_on` on the function would create a cycle with the existing `function_name` reference; the fix is to compute the log-group name from a local (e.g. "/aws/lambda/${var.config.prefix}-webhook") instead of referencing the function, then add `depends_on = [aws_cloudwatch_log_group.webhook]` to aws_lambda_function.webhook.
